content:
Samantha Lee: hey folks — need help w/ customer-facing explanation. We have a ticket where the customer says Console “Cost breakdown” doesn’t match invoice total (off by ~8% on a day). What’s the recommended way to explain the difference + where can I point them internally so I’m not freelancing wording?

SupportBot: Linked Jira: SUP-31844-console-cost-breakdown-does-not-match-invoice (internal)

Chloe Martin: yep, we’ve seen this during the transition. Key thing: invoice = source of truth for billable amount; Console cost breakdown is an attribution view and (depending on org / env) may be powered by the new standard cost model behind a flag.

Chloe Martin: for customer wording, I’d keep it simple:
- Console breakdown is a *per-request attribution estimate* (prefill/decode, cache effects, etc.) and can include categories that don’t map 1:1 to invoice line items.
- Invoice totals include billing-specific adjustments (plan/contract pricing, credits/discounts, rounding, minimums/commits) and are aggregated on billing windows.
- In some periods there can be timing differences due to telemetry lag/backfills.

Chloe Martin: internal reference: Confluence “Cost breakdown taxonomy” + the field semantics doc (links below from Elliot). That doc has the exact definitions for “request-attributable” vs “allocated overhead”.

Nadia Rahman: +1. Also: Console might show *token-attributed compute* but invoice may include non-token costs depending on contract (e.g., dedicated capacity / reserved commits). For hosted usage it should be closer, but still:
- Console uses observed token counts split into `prefill_tokens` and `decode_tokens` + cache hits/misses.
- Invoice doesn’t itemize prefill vs decode; it’s priced per-token (or per-unit) under contract.
- Cache: Console may show “effective cost after cache” vs “raw compute cost” depending on the view. That’s where % deltas show up.

Samantha Lee: ok so for customer: “Console is attribution/observability, invoice is billing record” + mention time window + adjustments. Anything specific about overhead?

Laura Bennett: yes please call out overhead carefully. Our guidance:
- In Console, “Overhead (allocated)” is an internal allocation of shared infra (control plane, idle/buffer capacity, etc.) for unit economics transparency.
- Invoices generally do NOT bill customers an “overhead” line item; pricing already embeds those costs implicitly.
- So if the customer is summing every Console category to compare to invoice, they may be mixing “request-attributable” + “allocated overhead”. That can easily create a mismatch.

Laura Bennett: Suggested customer phrasing (short):
“Console shows operational cost attribution categories, including some internal allocations used for monitoring and optimization. Your invoice reflects billable usage per your contract terms and is the system of record.”

Elliot Price: dropping the internal docs that support can use for consistent language:
- Field semantics / taxonomy (internal): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ARCH/ADR-022+Cost+Breakdown+Taxonomy
- Standard cost model PRD (internal): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/PROD/Standard+Cost+Model+PRD
- Console guidance (internal how-to): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENG/Integrating+Console+with+Cost+Model+API

Elliot Price: also the docs snippet we’ve been using internally (paste-able in support responses w/ light edits):
“Cost breakdowns in Console are designed for attribution and optimization (e.g., understanding prefill vs decode, cache impact, batching efficiency). Billing invoices are calculated from billing meters and contract terms (credits/discounts, rounding, minimum commitments) and may not match Console category sums exactly. If there is a large or persistent discrepancy, we can investigate telemetry lag or cost-model drift.”

Rafael Mendes: from SRE side: if they’re claiming a big mismatch, ask for:
- org + project + date range + region
- whether they’re looking at “Allocated overhead” included
- screenshot of the Console breakdown view
Then we can check drift dashboards. Common causes we’ve seen:
1) telemetry lag/backfill on token metering
2) schema-version mismatch during rollout (Console calling cost-model v1 vs older billing primitive path)
3) customer comparing different windows (UTC vs local / invoice cycle)

Rafael Mendes: internal links:
- Drift dashboard: https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/cost-model-drift
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SRE/Cost+Model+API+Incident+Runbook

Samantha Lee: super helpful. I’ll respond to customer w/ the “attribution vs billing record” + make sure they’re not adding allocated overhead. If they still see mismatch after aligning window/filters, I’ll collect details + loop back w/ drift dashboard checks.

Chloe Martin: one more nuance: if they’re on Dedicated, invoice is usually commit-based, so per-request attribution can look “higher/lower” day-to-day because we’re allocating reserved capacity across usage. That’s expected.

Samantha Lee: got it — this one is hosted (API), but good call. Thanks all.
